acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC in seven accessions between 2021 and 2024 and was ingested by the RAC as Accessions 2021:088, 2021:094, 2021:118, 2023:023, 2023:050, 2024:008, and 2024:034.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Collection is comprised of five series.
Original order was maintained as much as possible.
The collection arrangement is as follows:

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the office files Barry Gaberman created throughout his career at the Ford Foundation. Gaberman worked at the Foundation for over 30 years and served in various positions, including Senior Vice President from 1996 to 2006. Gaberman's files are organized into 5 different series. The series are based on the type of record they contain.

Chronology files are contained in the collection's first series. They compile Gaberman's outgoing correspondence in chronological order. The second series contains trips and meetings files, and the third series contains reports and other papers. A small set of files pertaining to administration of the Foundation's field offices comprises the fourth series. Lastly, Series 5 contains Gaberman's subject files.

Gaberman's office files help document the activities and program interests of the various Ford Foundation programs in which he served between the 1970s and 1980s. The programs include the Foundation's Asia and Pacific Program, Program Related Investments (PRI), and United States and International Affairs Programs (USIAP). Files Gaberman created throughout his Vice President positions in the Program Division and the Office of the President regard program administration as well as broad Foundation interests and projects like supporting the expanding nonprofit sector, the philanthropic response to the September 11 Terrorist Attack, and the United Nations World Conference Against Racism (WCAR) and its aftermath.

Other common material formats found throughout the collection include memos, drafts, notes, agendas, itineraries, briefing books, articles, press clippings, publications, and grant action records. There is also some audiovisual material.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research with select materials restricted as noted.
RAC provides an access surrogate of digital media and born-digital files, not the original files. To request an access surrogate be made, please contact a RAC archivist.
When requesting to view audiovisual material, please check the "Access" note for each Title. If a Title does not currently have an access copy, please contact a RAC archivist for further instruction.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Files in the series are arranged by chronological order.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains the chronology files Barry Gaberman created throughout his multiple positions at the Ford Foundation. The chronology files hold Gaberman's outgoing correspondence organized by year. Most of the files in the series also have their contents ordered alphabetically by the name of the addressee.
The chronology files span across most of Gaberman's career at the Foundation. They include correspondence Gaberman produced when he served in:
- Asia and Pacific Program (Assistant Program Officer; Program Officer) - 1976-1980
- Program Related Investments (PRI) (Program Officer in Charge) - 1982
- United States and International Affairs Program (USIAP) (Program Officer in Charge; Deputy Vice President) - 1983-1989
- Program Division, Deputy Vice President – 1990-1996
- Office of the President, Senior Vice President - 1996-2006

The files include correspondence Gaberman sent within the Ford Foundation and correspondence he sent to external individuals and organizations. There are a few smaller items like articles and grant action records inserted amongst the correspondence.

Gaberman's correspondence highlights job duties he performed and program activities of the specific positions he held. Population and family planning in the countries of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh were major areas of focus when he worked in the Asia and Pacific Program. Healthcare, nutrition, and refugees are other topics discussed within the correspondence he produced at that time.

Files show how Gaberman's focus shifted to Program Related Investment loans and requests when he served as Program Officer in Charge of PRI. Economic development and the arts are some of the program areas highlighted in Gaberman's correspondence from his years as Program Officer in Charge and Deputy Vice President of USIAP.

Lastly, throughout Gaberman's positions as Deputy Vice President in the Program Division and Senior Vice President in the Office of the President, his responsibilities centered around program administration and strategy for the Foundation. Correspondence from these roles also concern broad Foundation interests and initiatives like global philanthropy and the expanding nonprofit sector.

Trips and meetings files

physdesc.extent: 17 document boxes: 16 letter boxes and 1 legal box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains trips and meetings files Barry Gaberman created and maintained when he worked at the Ford Foundation. The files in the series specifically originate from Gaberman's positions as Deputy Vice President in the Program Division (1990-1996) and Senior Vice President in the Office of the President (1996-2006).

Within the series, there are a few main types of meetings and trips documented. There are internal Ford Foundation staff meetings, country visits and visits to Foundation field offices, and external meetings concerning philanthropy and the nonprofit sector.
Gaberman's trips to the Foundation's field offices encompassed office audits and site visits. They give insight into these offices' administration and programming.

Reports

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains reports and other papers Barry Gaberman collected when he worked at the Ford Foundation. The reports cover a wide range of subjects related to Foundation program interests and activities, grants, and history. Many reports were discussion papers for Foundation Board of Trustees meetings. Other papers in the series are materials produced for meetings, administrative documentation, and program decision documentation. There are also files containing groupings of publications and press clippings around specific projects like the Innovations in American Government Awards Program.

Many of the reports in the series are copies of reports contained in the Ford Foundation records, Catalogued Reports collection. In instances of exact duplicates, reports in the Gaberman collection have been removed. These files are identified with the #000000 catalogued report number in the title.

Several of these reports include additional documents that may provide greater context for users. For files containing these reports, scope and content notes have been added giving the #000000 catalogued report number so that users can also access them in that collection.

scopecontent.p: This series contains a small set of files pertaining to administration of the Ford Foundation's field offices. Gaberman created these files during his Vice President positions at the Foundation. The files chiefly concern the programming, operations, and country specific contexts of the regional offices documented within the series. These specific offices were in the Foundation's Asia and Africa programs.
Correspondence, memos, press clippings, papers, and meeting materials make up the files.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files Barry Gaberman created and maintained when he worked at the Ford Foundation. They primarily originate from when Gaberman worked in the United States and International Affairs Programs (USAIP) and served in differed Vice President positions. The files concern grants, initiatives, consultancies, and some meetings.

The subject files Gaberman created provide insight into Foundation's interest and activity in the global nonprofit sector, the philanthropic response to the September 11 Terrorist Attack, combatting religious bigotry, and the United Nations World Conference Against Racism (WCAR) and its aftermath.
There are a few documents in the series that originate from after Gaberman left the Foundation.
